title: Lecture 13 · ATP and cellular energy management

blocks.html:
What to know

  • ATP is the shared energy currency. Its terminal phosphoanhydride bond releases about 30 kJ/mol under cellular conditions, enough to drive many reactions.
  • The ATP pool turns over rapidly. A cell has only seconds to minutes of ATP, so production and consumption must be matched continuously.
  • Phosphocreatine buffers sudden demand. Creatine kinase transfers a phosphate from phosphocreatine to ADP during the first seconds of intense exercise.
  • Energy charge reports the balance. (ATP + 0.5 ADP) / (ATP + ADP + AMP) falls when work outruns production; AMPK senses the rise in AMP and switches on catabolism.
  • Exercise changes the mix. Sprinting relies on phosphocreatine and glycolysis; sustained exercise relies more on oxidative phosphorylation and fat oxidation.

Check

check.question: Which system supplies ATP most rapidly during a short sprint?
check.explanation: The phosphocreatine system and anaerobic glycolysis can regenerate ATP within seconds, before oxidative metabolism ramps up.
